1. 다니엘과 같은 시대 선지자 에스겔의 소명: 1. The Call of Ezekiel, a Prophet of the Same Era as Daniel
지금 1차 포로로 끌려갔고, 2차, 3차 또 끌려 가야하거든요? 앞으로: Right now the first group has been taken into Exile, and a second and third group still have to be taken, right?  To the Jews who are going to be taken captive in the future,
고국에서는 예레미야가, 바벨론에서는 에스겔이 하나님의 말씀을 전하는거예요: Jeremiah back home, and Ezekiel in Babylon, are delivering God's word.
In about 7 years, Jerusalem is going to fall.
백성들은 설마 나라가 망할까?: The people think, surely the nation won't fall?
우리가 뭘 그렇게 잘 못 했지?: What did we do that was so wrong?
예루살렘에 성전이 있으니까 우리는 돌아가게 될 거다: There's a temple in Jerusalem, so we'll get to go back
To people like this, he explains why God brought them into Exile.
예레미야는 왜 끌려가야 하는지를 설명하고,: Jeremiah explains why they have to be taken away,
다니엘은 끌려가서 어떤 것들을 배웠는지 설명하고,: Daniel explains what they learned after being taken away,
에스겔은 왜 끌려왔는지 설명한다. 됐죠?: Ezekiel explains why they were taken away. Got it?
이렇게 하면 책의 성격이 확 보이잖아요?: When you put it like this, the character of each book jumps right out, doesn't it?
어찌 보면 이런 말씀들도 기록으로 남겨서 앞으로 오고오는 모든 세대 사람: In a way, these words were also left on record to show all the generations to come that things happen just as God's word says.
당대의 그 사람들은 이런 말씀을 듣지 않습니다. 예레미야 보세요. 아무도: The people of that day don't listen to these words. Look at Jeremiah. He preaches for 40 years and nobody listens!
So the Bible is like a love letter God wrote to you.
So listen carefully.
1) The Call of Ezekiel
 - The first Exile was in B.C 606, and Ezekiel seems to have been taken to Babylon in the second Exile, in B.C 597, at about 25 years old.
<겔1:1~2> 제 삼십 년 사월 오일에 내가 그발 강 가: <Ezek 1:1~2> Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I was by the river of Chebar
사로잡힌 자 중에 있더니 하늘이 열리며 하나님의 이상을 내게 보이시니 여:
among the captives, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God. In the fifth day of the month, which was the fifth year of king Jehoiachin's captivity
 - He was taken along with King Jehoiachin when the king was taken captive. 'The thirtieth year' could be interpreted in several ways, but hardly any of them fit; it makes sense if it means he was 30 years old. God usually calls people and uses them at 30. Jesus was thirty, John the Baptist was thirty, Jeremiah was thirty, Zechariah was thirty.
<겔1:3> 갈대아 땅 그발 강 가에서 여호와의 말씀이 부시의 아들 제사:
<Ezek 1:3> The word of the LORD came expressly unto me, Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the LORD was upon me
 - Ezekiel received his call while he was in captivity in the second Exile, so he delivered the word to the people who were in captivity.
에스겔서를 모르면 하나님의 심정을 제대로 읽었다 할 수 없음. 바벨론 포:
If you don't know Ezekiel, you can't say you've really read God's heart. It's a very important book for understanding what God's heart was like during the Babylonian Exile.
 - Ezekiel doesn't minister with words alone; he ministers by doing all kinds of strange things that grab people's attention.
 2) God Strengthens Ezekiel
<겔3:8~9> 내가 그들의 얼굴을 대하도록 네 얼굴을 굳게 하였고 그들:
<Ezek 3:8~9> Behold, I have made thy face strong against their faces, and thy forehead strong against their foreheads. As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead: fear them not, neither be dismayed at their looks, though they be a rebellious house.
 - Because the times are evil, he has to go through intense training, and his face has to be made hard — diamond, harder than granite — to do the ministry.
그만큼 에스겔 당시의 시대가 악했다는 것. 하나님의 일을 하는 사람은 작: That's how evil the times were in Ezekiel's day. A person doing God's work can't do it well if he gets hurt too easily over little things. There's just so much that hurts...
자신들의 죄가 없지는 않지만 그리 크지는 않은 것 같다고 생각: They thought their sins weren't zero, but didn't seem all that big
3) 에스겔서 안에서 하나님께서 진노하시는 이유(포로 된 사람들의 오해): 3) Why God Is Angry in the Book of Ezekiel (the misunderstandings of the people in Exile)
1. 전능하신 하나님을 오해했다. 나라가 망하고 혼쭐나고도 인간들이 짧은: 1. They misunderstood the almighty God. Even after the nation fell and they got a hard lesson, people with their shortsighted thinking misunderstand God
2.자신들의 죄가 없지는 않지만 그리 크지는 않은 것 같다고 생각: 2. They thought their sins weren't zero, but didn't seem all that big
3.조상들이 포도를 많이 먹어서 자기들의 이가 시다고 생각하며: 3. They thought their ancestors had eaten lots of grapes and that's why their teeth were set on edge
4. They despaired that they had no hope.
5. They thought what God did was unfair.
바벨론이 우리보다 훨씬 악독한데 이기게 하고 우리는 지게 하는 하나님이: They thought God was unfair for letting Babylon, which was far more wicked than they were, win, and making them lose. (Habakkuk)
2. 에스겔서 24장까지의 내용: 2. The Content of Ezekiel up to Chapter 24
1~3장) 에스겔의 소명 장면\n - 신비하고 장엄하고 특이함. 특히 소:
Chapters 1~3) The scene of Ezekiel's call
 - Mysterious, majestic, and strange. Especially in the call scene, he talks about certain living creatures — an unidentified flying object. You wonder what they are, but if you keep reading, you find out.
이건 나중에 10장 가서 정체가 드러난다. 케루빔이라는 천사예요. 성경에: Their identity is revealed later, in chapter 10. They're angels called cherubim. In the Bible it says cherubims.
우리는 천사 하면 대개 이런 모습 떠올리죠?: When we think of angels, we usually picture something like this, right?
천사 중에 여자는 없습니다. 물로 남자도 없죠. 우린 엄청 예쁘면 천사같: There are no female angels. Of course, there are no male ones either. When someone is really pretty, we say she's like an angel, right?
천사가 예쁜 여자처럼 생긴게 아니예요. 어떤 것은 소 같고, 어떤 것은: Angels don't look like pretty women. Some look like an ox, some look like an eagle, like that. Some look like a person.
천사들이 오히려 그러죠. 걔중에 좀 괜찮은 천사가 있으면 ‘와~사람 같다: If anything, the angels say it the other way around. If there's an angel among them who's kind of good-looking, they go, ‘Wow~ looks like a human.’
Anyway, Ezekiel sees a really strange sight.
이런 비행물체를 봤는데 번개처럼 여기 저기 왔다갔다 얼마나 빠른지 목적: He saw this flying object, and it went back and forth like lightning — so fast, straight to its destination, zoom~ gone.
That's what it says up to verse 21.
그리고 22절부터 쭉 보면: And if you keep reading from verse 22,
이런 모습을 봤다는 얘기고요: he's saying he saw something that looked like this
2장에 가면 하나님께서 에스겔에게 단단히 주의를 시킵니다. 이 백성은 패: In chapter 2, God gives Ezekiel a firm warning. This people is a rebellious house, a thick-skinned bunch. But you don't need to be afraid of them. Open your mouth and eat what I give you
그래서 보니까 한 손이 두루마리 하나를 주는데 그 안에는 애곡과 재앙의: So he looked, and a hand was handing him a scroll, and written inside were words of lamentation and woe.
3장에는 그 두루마리를 먹으라 하는 말씀을 하시는데 먹었더니 꿀처럼 맛있: In chapter 3 He tells him to eat that scroll, and he says when he ate it, it was as sweet as honey. Want to try some?
여러분 여러분이 글씨를 읽었는데 그게 하나님의 말씀으로 들리잖아요? 그럼: Friends, when you read the words and they come to you as the word of God, right? Then it really is sweet as honey.
저는 이게 비유인 줄 알았어요: I thought this was a figure of speech
근데 아니라. 제가 하나님을 만나고 나서 레위기를 읽는데 주체할 수 없이: But it wasn't. After I met God, I was reading Leviticus and the tears just poured out, I couldn't stop them.
내 소원이 하나님 사랑한다고 자신있게 말해 보는거였는데, 레위기 속에 나: My wish was to be able to say with confidence that I love God, and the God who appeared in Leviticus was such a lovely God, caring so carefully for orphans and widows and the powerless.
그렇게 성경을 읽어 나가는데 정말로 입안에서 단내음이 나는거예요. 깜짝: As I kept reading the Bible like that, my mouth really tasted sweet. I was shocked. So this wasn't a figure of speech...
그래서 하나님께서 에스겔에게 내가 너를 필리핀으로 보내는 것도 아니고 언: So God tells Ezekiel, I'm not sending you to the Philippines, and it's not a different language. They're your own people, so don't worry.
I've made your forehead like diamond, so don't be afraid even of a rebellious house. In other words, He gave him a face of iron.
그러니까 가서 11절 듣든지 아니 듣든지 여호와의 말씀이 이러하시다 하: So go, verse 11, and say, Thus saith the Lord GOD, whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.
저도 같은 심정으로 하고 있어요. 제 말들이, 엄밀히 말하면 제 말이 아: I do this with the same heart. My words, strictly speaking, aren't my words. There will be people who hear God's word in them and people who don't, but I don't worry about that; I just pass on, 'This is what God's word says.'
14절 보세요. 주의 영이 에스겔을 들어올려 데리고 가십니다. 근데 근심: Look at verse 14. The spirit of the Lord lifts Ezekiel up and takes him away. But it says he went in bitterness, in the heat of his spirit. Being troubled I can understand, but why would he be angry?
God handles Ezekiel a bit roughly. We'll see in a moment.
17절 여기 ‘인자야’ 라는 말이 나오는데 하나님께서 에스겔을 인자라고: Verse 17, here the phrase ‘Son of man’ comes up — God calls Ezekiel son of man. This isn't an ordinary expression.
한자 그대로 풀이하면 ‘사람의 아들’이라는 건데 옛날에 우리 할아버지들이: If you unpack the Chinese characters literally, it means ‘son of a human,’ and when our grandfathers translated it long ago, they rendered the Hebrew ‘ben adam’ word for word.
극존칭으로 하면 ‘인간의 자제 분이시여’: In the most honorific form: ‘O esteemed offspring of humankind’
조금 하대하면 ‘사람의 자식아’: A little lower: ‘you child of man’
하나님이 에스겔에게 높임말을 쓸 이유도 없고, 그렇다고 사람 새꺄라고 하: God has no reason to use honorifics with Ezekiel, but calling him ‘human brat’ is a bit much too
하나님이 화가 나서 지금 에스겔을 부르는 건데 그 분위기 대로라면 ‘사람: God is calling Ezekiel while He's angry, so going by that mood, it's right to translate it as something like ‘you child of man.’
Verses 17-19, just skim through them with your eyes. See what the mood is...
‘이 사람의 자식아 너를 이스라엘의 파수꾼으로 세웠어. 니가 가서 전했는: ‘You child of man, I've set you as a watchman for Israel. If you go and tell them and they don't listen, okay. But if they die because you didn't tell them, I'll kill you too.’
그래서 또 무슨 말씀 하시냐 하면 너 돌아가면 사람들이 너를 밧줄로 묶을: And what else does He say? When you go back, people will tie you up with ropes. But I'll make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so you can't speak. In case you say something and they come to their senses and turn back. Those guys are rebels.
여기 보세요. 이사야를 부르신 소명이 뭐예요? 이 백성들로 하여금 듣지도: Look here. What was Isaiah's call? Make this people unable to hear and unable to see. I'm afraid those wretches deserving death might come to their senses and turn back.
헛 된 말을 지절거리고 제사도 귀찮아서 아무 제물이나 가지고 와서 형식: Babbling empty words, too lazy even about sacrifices so they bring just any offering and only go through the motions of religion — I wish someone would shut the temple doors so I wouldn't have to look at them.
스바냐 보세요. 그런 짓거리를 하면서도 우리가 구원을 받았습니다!! 하는: Look at Zephaniah. Doing all that, and still shouting, We are saved!! — I'll kill every one of those wicked people.
Listen to God's heart as it comes through the prophets of the same era.
여러분 지금 하나님의 심정이 이 정도예요. 얼마나 사무쳤는지....내가: Friends, this is how God's heart is right now. How deeply it's gnawing at Him.... I'm God, I'm almighty, and nothing is working. Can you feel that helplessness and anger?
4장에는 390일 동안 인분 불에 빵을 구워서 먹으면서 예언하라는 말씀을: In chapter 4 He tells him to prophesy while baking and eating bread over a fire of human dung for 390 days.
인분이 똥이죠? 똥을 잘 말리면 불에 잘 탑니다. 지금도 유목민들은 소똥: Human dung is poop, right? If you dry poop well, it burns well. Even today nomads dry cow dung or horse dung and use it as fuel.
화력이 좋아요. 저도 몽골 선교 갔을 때 봤는데 이게 잘 말려야지 조금이: It burns hot. I saw it when I went on a mission trip to Mongolia — you have to dry it really well; if you burn some that's even a little underdried, the fragrance is overpowering.
They pick this stuff up and make a fire with it.
인도에 가면 소똥 축제가 있어요. 여러분 제가 여기 꼭 한 번 데려가고: In India there's a cow dung festival. Friends, I'd love to take you there sometime.
They make a fire like this and cook food and so on.
But Ezekiel is told to use human dung.
에스겔이 펄쩍 뛰죠. 아니고 하나님 제 평생 그런 부정한 걸 먹어 본적이: Ezekiel nearly jumps out of his skin. No, Lord, I've never eaten anything so unclean in my whole life. Please, I beseech Your Majesty, take this into consideration.
이게 무슨 뜻이냐? 에스겔을 몸으로 설교한다고 했죠? 패역한 이스라엘 백: What does this mean? We said Ezekiel preaches with his body, right? The rebellious Israelites won't listen when you just tell them, so Jeremiah too, Ezekiel too, they all show it with their bodies.
에스겔이 소똥으로 빵을 구원 먹고 있으면 동네 사람 다 몰려 오겟죠?: If Ezekiel is baking bread over cow dung and eating it, the whole neighborhood will come flocking, right?
가만 있어봐. 이 원초적인 향기가 어디서 오는거냐? 이 태초의 구린내 정: Wait a minute. Where is this primal fragrance coming from? What is this primordial stench...they say,
와 보니 에스겔이 소똥 냄새로 훈제한 빵을 먹고 있으니까 너 이게 뭐하는: and they come and see Ezekiel eating bread smoked with the smell of cow dung, so they'll ask, What on earth are you doing?
응 너네도 곧 먹을거야~: Oh, you'll be eating this soon too~
앞으로 이 백성들이 얼마나 부정한 음식들을 먹으며 비참하게 살게 될지 미: It's showing ahead of time how miserably this people will live, eating unclean food.
16절에 떡을 달아서 먹는다... 저울에 달아서 먹는다는 표현인데 이건: In verse 16 it says they eat bread by weight... eating it weighed on a scale — that's picture language
빵이 너무 부족하니까 까닥하면 살인나거든요? 그러니까 저울에 달아서 나눠: Bread is so scarce that one wrong move and someone gets killed, right? So weighing it on a scale to share it — it's picture language for a severe famine
5장) 세 가지 멸망의 예언\n - 몸에 있는 털을 다 뜯어서 3분의 1:
Chapter 5) Prophecy of three kinds of destruction
 - He's told to pull out all the hair on his body, strike a third with the sword and cut it up and scatter it, burn another third, and scatter another third when the wind blows.
사람의 수염이나 털이 그 사람에게 속한 것처럼 다 내게 속한 건데 내가: Just as a person's beard or hair belongs to him, they all belong to Me, and I'll pluck them all out, strike them with the sword, burn them with fire, scatter them among all the nations, and chase after those who flee until every one of them dies.
우리 봤죠? 앗수르가 사마리아 사람들 다 잡아다가 전 세계에 흩어 버리잖: We saw this, right? Assyria captured all the people of Samaria and scattered them all over the world, didn't it?
바벨론이라는 칼로 사람들 다 쳐 죽이고,: With the sword called Babylon, He strikes the people down,
예루살렘을 불 타버리고... 그 거리를 걸으며 쓴 예레미야 애가를 봤잖아: and Jerusalem burns... We saw Lamentations, which Jeremiah wrote walking through those streets.
6장) 하나님의 심판\n - 하나님의 말씀을 거역하고 맺은 언약을 위반한:
Chapter 6) God's Judgment
 - He proclaims that Israel, which rebelled against God's word and broke the covenant it made, will be destroyed,
and He tells Ezekiel to clap his hands and stamp his feet as he proclaims it. Anyway, to get their attention...
The time is come, the day is near.
볼지어다. 그 날이로다. 하면서 임박한 심판을 말해요.\n - B.C 5:
Behold, the day. That's how He speaks of the coming judgment.
 - He was taken captive in B.C 597 and called in 592, so the fall in 586 is only 5~6 years away.
8장) 예루살렘의 죄악상을 보여주시다: Chapter 8) God Shows Him the Sins of Jerusalem
<겔8:1~3> 제 육 년 유월 오일에 나는 집에 앉았고 유다 장로들은:
<Ezek 8:1~3> And it came to pass in the sixth year, in the sixth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I sat in mine house, and the elders of Judah sat before me, that the hand of the Lord GOD fell there upon me. Then I beheld, and lo a likeness as the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins even downward, fire; and from his loins even upward, as the appearance of brightness, as the colour of amber. And he put forth the form of an hand, and took me by a lock of mine head; and the spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, and brought me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the door of the inner gate that looketh toward the north; where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provoketh to jealousy.
 - A very strange scene, like at his call.
에스겔 뜰에 유다 장로들이 꾸역 꾸역 찾아와서 하나님께서 왜 이렇게 우리: The elders of Judah came crowding into Ezekiel's yard to ask, in a nasty, accusing way, why God had ruined them like this and what they had done wrong.
But young Ezekiel isn't prepared, so he's in no position to answer.
다급한 하나님께서 이상한 비행물체를 타고 내려오셔서 사람의 손 같은 것이: God, in a hurry, comes down on that strange flying object, and something like a human hand shoots out and pulls out Ezekiel's spirit,
and this is the scene where He takes him all over Jerusalem and shows him the sins of Jerusalem.
<겔8:4~5> 이스라엘 하나님의 영광이 거기 있는데 내가 들에서 보던: <Ezek 8:4~5> And, behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, according to the vision that I saw in the plain. Then said he unto me, Son of man, lift up thine eyes now the way toward the north. So I lifted up mine eyes the way toward the north, and behold northward at the gate of the altar this image of jealousy in the entry.
지금 상황이 하나님께서 진노하셔서 에스겔을 옆에 태운다든지 손을 잡고 간: Here's the situation: God is furious, so He's not seating Ezekiel beside Him or taking him by the hand — He roughly drags him around by the hair, showing him the sins all over Jerusalem.
사람이라면 쳐다만 봐도 화가나는 그런 심정.\n - 하나님께서도 진노하시:
The kind of feeling where, if you were a person, just looking at it would make you angry.
 - When God is angry, He speaks very harshly too. Jesus didn't say to the scribes, priests, and Pharisees, ‘O esteemed offspring of vipers’; He said, ‘You brood of vipers!’

역사적으로 하나님께서 떠나신 후에는 항상 외국 군대가 와서 예루살렘을 삼: Historically, after God left, a foreign army always came and swallowed Jerusalem.

남자는 아내 말고 다른 여자와 성행위를 해야하고, 여자도 마찬가지. 그: A man had to have sex with a woman other than his wife, and the same for women. 근데 그게 아니다. 모든 사람은 자기 죄로 인해서만 죄값을 받는다. 그: But that's not so. Every person pays the price only for his own sin. Never use that nonsense proverb again, He says

이런 걸 볼 때마다 하나님의 견인. 우리 기독교 교리 중에 ‘성도의 견인: Every time I see this, God's perseverance. Among our Christian doctrines there's a doctrine called ‘the perseverance of the saints.’

19장) 애가 – 슬픈노래\n - 하나님의 최고장을 받고도 안 돌아 오니:
Chapter 19) Lamentation – a Sad Song

 - This sword is the army the king of Babylon brings. So that no nation can stop Babylon — a sword furbished to be very swift and very sharp, that's Babylon, and with this sword He will cut off the head of the harlot Jerusalem.
<겔21:18~23> 여호와의 말씀이 내게 임하여 가라사대 인자야 너는:
<Ezek 21:18~23> The word of the LORD came unto me again, saying, Also, thou son of man, appoint thee two ways, that the sword of the king of Babylon may come: both twain shall come forth out of one land: and choose thou a place, choose it at the head of the way to the city. Appoint a way, that the sword may come to Rabbath of the Ammonites, and to Judah in Jerusalem the defenced. For the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination: he made his arrows bright, he consulted with images, he looked in the liver. At his right hand was the divination for Jerusalem, to appoint captains, to open the mouth in the slaughter, to lift up the voice with shouting, to appoint battering rams against the gates, to cast a mount, and to build a fort. And it shall be unto them as a false divination in their sight, to them that have sworn oaths: but he will call to remembrance the iniquity, that they may be taken.
 - The sword of the king of Babylon is coming toward Jerusalem, the road splits, and he casts lots to see which way to go.
자기 우상에게 바칠 희생제물의 간을 살펴보는데 파란색이면 왼쪽, 빨간색이: He examines the liver of the sacrifice to offer to his idol: if it's blue, left; if it's red, right.
그런데 빨간쪽이다. 그래서 예루살렘으로 가는 점괘를 확실히 얻었다고 하는: And it's the red side. So God gives Ezekiel a live broadcast of him getting a sure omen to go to Jerusalem.
Ezekiel is sitting in Babylon watching all of this.
이제 예루살렘 초토화는 정해졌다. 가차 없이 베어버리는, 끔직이도 사랑했: Now the devastation of Jerusalem is settled. Cutting her down without mercy — He's cutting down with His own hand the wife He loved so dearly. When love is betrayed, the sense of betrayal is all the greater. Because He loved her so much, He killed her with His own hand and ended it.
22~23장) 국문.\n - 하나님께서 창녀 예루살렘의 죄를 추궁하시는데:
Chapters 22~23) The Interrogation.
 - God presses the harlot Jerusalem about her sins, and the woman says she didn't sin.
그래서 처음부터 어떤 죄를 지었는지 다 이야기 해주시는 장면. 남편이 바: So it's the scene where He tells her every sin she committed from the very beginning. The husband had gathered plenty of evidence of her cheating.
근데 이 여자가 발뺌하니까 하나 하나 다 불러 주는거예요. 몇월 며칠 어: But since this woman denies it, He reads it all out one by one. On such-and-such a date, at such-and-such a place, you met so-and-so and did this.
결국 이 죄는 율법에 나와있는 내용이다. 율법서를 공부했다면 예루살렘이: In the end, these sins are things spelled out in the law. If you studied the books of the Law, you can understand why Jerusalem fell like this.
24장) 참수와 에스겔 아내의 죽음: Chapter 24) The Beheading and the Death of Ezekiel's Wife
<겔24:1~2> 제 구 년 시월 십일에 여호와의 말씀이 내게 임하여 가:
<Ezek 24:1~2> Again in the ninth year, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, Son of man, write thee the name of the day, even of this same day: the king of Babylon drew close to Jerusalem this same day.
 - The 9th year of Zedekiah, the 10th day, or the 9th year and 10th day after the second Exile. As a date, it's B.C 588, the 10th day of the 10th month. Now he has drawn close. He's prophesying a destruction that's right on top of them.
 - How angry God must have been: He compares the city of Jerusalem to a big cauldron, calls its nobles and people a flock of sheep, pours plenty of water into the cauldron and builds a fire under it, and then
다시 다 꺼내서 새로 물을 붓고 더 불을 피워서 다시 고기를 삶고 국물을: takes everything out again, pours in fresh water, makes the fire hotter, boils the meat again, boils down the broth, and burns the bones,
그래도 계속 달궈서 가마솥의 녹이 부스럭 부스럭 나와서 반질반질해질 정도: and still keeps heating it until the rust on the cauldron flakes off, crackle crackle, and it's shiny and smooth. This is God's wrath — He's showing a miniature of hell.
<겔24:15~17> 여호와의 말씀이 또 내게 임하여 가라사대 인자야 내:
<Ezek 24:15~17> Also the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, Son of man, behold, I take away from thee the desire of thine eyes with a stroke: yet neither shalt thou mourn nor weep, neither shall thy tears run down. Forbear to cry, make no mourning for the dead, bind the tire of thine head upon thee, and put on thy shoes upon thy feet, and cover not thy lips, and eat not the bread of men.
 - So to let Ezekiel know His heart — the heart of killing Jerusalem, stewing her long in the cauldron, and burning her in the fire until the rust comes off — God takes Ezekiel's wife.
‘내가 방금 사랑하는 아내의 목을 쳐 버렸어. 이 비통한 심정을 누가 알: ‘I just cut off the head of the wife I love. Who could understand this grief? If you're going to deliver My words, you have to know My heart too.’
여러분 호세아 생각나요? 바람 핀 아내를 자꾸 용서하고 데려와야 하는: Friends, remember Hosea?  Do you know how I feel, having to keep forgiving my cheating wife and bringing her back? You go marry a lewd woman too, a harlot who loves to cheat. And every time she cheats, go bring her back. And then come and deliver My words.
Eun-saem, don't doze off and get the wrong idea...
그래서 사람들이 에스겔의 아내가 갑자기 죽어버린 것을 보고 물으면 이 모: So when people see that Ezekiel's wife suddenly died and ask about it — all this pain, God suffers it, Ezekiel suffers it, and soon everyone will suffer it.
3. 열방을 향한 예언(25장~32장)\n - 하나님께서 진노하셔서 바벨:
3. Prophecies Against the Nations (chapters 25~32)
 - In His anger, God cut off Jerusalem's head with the furbished sword called Babylon.
Right when He's cut off His wife's head with His own hand, and the warm blood is dripping...drip...drip... from the flashing, gleaming sword,
고개를 들어 탁 보니까 여태까지 예루살렘이라는 창녀와 놀아난 건달들이 쭈: He lifts His head and looks, and there are the thugs who've been fooling around with the harlot called Jerusalem all this time, standing there awkwardly.
어떻게 되겠어요? 지금 내 아내의 목을 쳐 버렸는데 이까짓놈들 오늘 거리: What's going to happen? I just cut off my wife's head — if these punks so much as twitch today, they're dead, period.
칼을 든김에 모든 열방들을 쳐버리시는데 25장에 암몬, 모압, 에돔, 2:
With the sword already in hand, He strikes all the nations: Ammon, Moab, and Edom in chapter 25, Tyre in chapters 26~28, Sidon in chapter 28, Egypt in chapters 29~31 — striking whatever comes His way.
 - And then in chapter 32 He sweeps them all into one pit.
33장) 파수꾼의 사명\n - 백성이 말을 듣든지 아니 듣든지 가서 고하:
Chapter 33) The Watchman's Mission
 - He tells him to go and tell them whether the people listen or not.
네가 말을 했는데도 그 사람들이 회개하지 않으면 너는 책임이 없도 자기: If you spoke and those people didn't repent, you're not responsible, and they will die in their own iniquity, but
네가 외치지 않아서 사람이 죽었다면 그 사람은 자기 죄에 죽지만 그 피를: if someone died because you didn't cry out, that person dies in his own sin, but He said He would require his blood at your hand.
34장) 자기만 먹이는 이스라엘의 목자들: Chapter 34) The Shepherds of Israel Who Feed Only Themselves
양떼를 힘들게 해서 흩어지게 하는 목자들을 쳐서 예언함. 그래서 결국에는: He prophesies against the shepherds who wear out the flock and scatter it. And so in the end, instead of shepherds like these, He sets up one true shepherd, and that shepherd is David — and this speaks of our Jesus.
36장) 바벨론에서 돌이키신다: Chapter 36) He Brings Them Back from Babylon
<겔36:21~23> 그러나 이스라엘 족속이 들어간 그 열국에서 더럽힌:
<Ezek 36:21~23> But I had pity for mine holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the heathen, whither they went. Therefore say unto the house of Israel, thus saith the Lord GOD; I do not this for your sakes, O house of Israel, but for mine holy name's sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen, whither ye went. And I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the heathen, which ye have profaned in the midst of them; and the heathen shall know that I am the LORD, saith the Lord GOD, when I shall be sanctified in you before their eyes.
 - It's not because Israel had enough righteousness to be saved and restored; it's because of God's name — so that He Himself wouldn't be dishonored — He does it for His own sake.
그런데 하나님께서는 당신을 위해서 하시는데 은혜는 우리가 입는다. 우리는: But God does it for His own sake, and we're the ones who receive the grace. We say we live for others, but in reality we often live for ourselves. That's the difference
37장) 에스골 골짜기의 환상\n - 24장에서 푸욱 구워가지고 삶은 뼈:
Chapter 37) The Vision of the Valley of Bones
 - The bones that were boiled long and hard in chapter 24 and dumped out into the valley come back together and form a great army.
이미 죽어 완전히 온 세상에 흩어져 버렸던 유대인들을 다시 살려내서 본토: It means He'll bring the Jews, who had already died and been completely scattered all over the world, back to life and bring them back to their homeland. It's not talking about us.
38~39장) 곡과 마곡. 마지막 때의 전쟁\n - 그래서 마지막 전쟁을:
Chapters 38~39) Gog and Magog. The War of the Last Days
 - So there's a final war, and countries like the Soviet Union, Iran, Libya, Azerbaijan, and Armenia join forces with the anti-Western Arabs to prepare for war.
In the last days, you need to keep a close eye on the international news.
5. 회복 될 성전에 대한 환상(40~48장): 5. The Vision of the Temple to Be Restored (chapters 40~48)
이 부분이 에스겔에서 어려운 부분인데 회복될 성전의 규격과 모양 이런게: This is the hard part of Ezekiel — it gives the measurements and shape of the temple to be restored and so on, right? But there's nothing like it in Israel's history.
바벨론 포로에서 돌아와서 이루어질 일과도 맞지 않고, 오늘 교회와 맞추어: It doesn't fit what happened after the return from the Babylonian Exile, it doesn't fit at all if you match it to today's church, it doesn't fit if you match it to the Jews restored at the end of human history, and whether you match it to the millennial kingdom or to heaven, it doesn't apply — that kind of text.
Still, there's a slight clue in chapter 43.
<겔43:10~11> 인자야 너는 이 전을 이스라엘 족속에게 보여서 그들:
<Ezek 43:10~11> Thou son of man, shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern. And if they be ashamed of all that they have done, shew them the form of the house, and the fashion thereof, and the goings out thereof, and the comings in thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the laws thereof: and write it in their sight, that they may keep the whole form thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and do them.
 - There's a condition attached, 'if': if they are ashamed of all they have done, then teach them the form and fashion of this house.
조건절이 충족되지 않아 이루어 질 뻔 했다가 이루어지지 않은 그런 문제로: If you see it as something that almost came true but didn't, because the condition wasn't met, it gets resolved. It doesn't fall neatly into place, but there's room to interpret it this way.
그래서 거기 보면 뭐 발목, 허리, 머리 물이 차올라서 막 은혜의 강물이: So people look at the water coming up to the ankles, the waist, over the head there, and say the river of grace is overflowing, but there's not much basis for that.
We used to sing a lot of songs about water flowing from the throne and so on, right?
그리고 설사 이게 이루어진 일이라 하더라도 우리와는 상관 없는, 자신들의: And even if this were something that came true, it has nothing to do with us — it applies to the Jews who repented of their deeds and sins, not to us.
So that wraps up the latter part of Ezekiel, and we go on to 1 Chronicles.
